+  /// Each backend's second verb is its own named button, not a menu item. A menu holding exactly one

+  func testGitOffersAmendAsItsOwnButton() throws {

+    let amend = button(app, id: "commit.amend")

1	import SwiftUI
2	
3	/// Record a commit: what will be included, the message, and the failure when there is one.
4	///
5	/// **Why a dialog rather than a box in the Changes pane.** Measured against the pane it would have
6	/// lived in: the composer is ~152pt and `InspectorPanePolicy.expandedMinHeight` leaves 86pt of body,
7	/// so at the pane's own drag floor the Commit button was below the fold. At a default third of a
8	/// 900pt window it left two file rows for git and one for jj — for a list whose entire job is letting
9	/// you decide whether committing is safe. Pinning it would also have meant switching Changes to fill
10	/// hosting, which disables the documented compress-and-scroll valve (`InspectorSplitView`), so a
11	/// short window would clip the button rather than scroll to it.
12	///
13	/// The dialog also deletes state rather than managing it: the draft and the selection live here for
14	/// the sheet's lifetime, so there is no per-workroom draft store to prune on delete, no recycled
15	/// workroom name inheriting last week's message, and no two windows racing one `Defaults` dictionary
16	/// (`AppStore` is per window).
17	///
18	/// The cost, accepted: this covers the diff you were reading.
19	struct CommitSheet: View {
20	  let pending: PendingCommit
21	  let onDismiss: () -> Void
22	
23	  @EnvironmentObject var store: AppStore
24	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
25	
26	  @State private var summary = ""
27	  @State private var messageBody = ""
28	  /// EXCLUSIONS, not selections — see `CommitDraft.selected(from:excluding:)`. A file written while
29	  /// this sheet is open arrives checked; a file the user unticked stays unticked.
30	  @State private var excluded: Set<String> = []
31	  @State private var phase: Phase = .editing
32	  @State private var prefilled = false
33	  @FocusState private var summaryFocused: Bool
34	
35	  private enum Phase: Equatable {
36	    case editing
37	    /// Selected paths whose staged content this commit would discard, awaiting confirmation.
38	    case confirmingStagedLoss([String])
39	    case committing
40	    case failed(VCSFailureDialog)
41	  }
42	
43	  private var isJJ: Bool { pending.vcs == "jj" }
44	  private var status: WorkroomStatus? { store.workroomStatuses[pending.sid] }
45	
46	  /// Every changed file, from whichever shape this backend reports.
47	  private var files: [ChangedFile] {
48	    guard let status else { return [] }
49	    if let workingCopy = status.jjWorkingCopy { return workingCopy.files }
50	    return status.changedFiles ?? []
51	  }
52	
53	  private var selectedFiles: [ChangedFile] {
54	    // jj commits the whole change, so the exclusion set is never applied to it.
55	    isJJ ? files : CommitDraft.selected(from: files, excluding: excluded)
56	  }
57	
58	  private var blockedReason: String? {
59	    CommitDraft.blockedReason(
60	      vcs: pending.vcs, summary: summary, selectedCount: selectedFiles.count,
61	      totalCount: files.count, conflicted: status?.conflicted ?? false, sequencer: nil)
62	  }
63	
64	  var body: some View {
65	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 14) {
66	      header
67	      fileSection
68	      messageSection
69	      if case .confirmingStagedLoss(let paths) = phase { stagedLossNotice(paths) }
70	      if case .failed(let dialog) = phase { CommitFailureNotice(dialog: dialog) }
71	      Divider()
72	      buttons
73	    }
74	    .padding(20)
75	    .frame(width: 520)
76	    .onAppear(perform: prefill)
77	    // `children: .contain` is load-bearing: an identifier on a plain container makes SwiftUI treat it
78	    // as ONE element and swallow everything inside, which XCUITest then cannot reach. Same lesson
79	    // `VCSFailureSheet` records.
80	    .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
81	    .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.sheet")
82	  }
83	
84	  private var header: some View {
85	    HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 8) {
86	      Text(isJJ ? "Describe this change" : "Commit changes")
87	        .font(.headline)
88	        .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.title")
89	      Spacer(minLength: 0)
90	      if !files.isEmpty {
91	        Text(countCaption)
92	          .font(.caption)
93	          .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
94	          .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.count")
95	      }
96	    }
97	  }
98	
99	  /// The primary button's label, which becomes an explicit confirmation while the staged-work
100	  /// warning is up so it can never read as an ordinary Commit.
101	  private var primaryLabel: String {
102	    if case .confirmingStagedLoss = phase { return "Commit anyway" }
103	    return CommitDraft.commitLabel(selectedCount: selectedFiles.count, vcs: pending.vcs)
104	  }
105	
106	  private var countCaption: String {
107	    isJJ
108	      ? "\(files.count) file\(files.count == 1 ? "" : "s") in this change"
109	      : "\(selectedFiles.count) of \(files.count) file\(files.count == 1 ? "" : "s")"
110	  }
111	
112	  // MARK: Files
113	
114	  @ViewBuilder private var fileSection: some View {
115	    if files.isEmpty {
116	      // jj can legitimately describe an empty change, so this is a note rather than a blocker there.
117	      Text(
118	        isJJ
119	          ? "This change has no file changes yet. You can still give it a message."
120	          : "Nothing has changed in this workroom yet."
121	      )
122	      .font(.callout).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
123	      .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
124	    } else {
125	      VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
126	        if !isJJ { selectAllRow }
127	        ScrollView {
128	          VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 2) {
129	            ForEach(files) { file in
130	              CommitFileRow(
131	                file: file, showsCheckbox: !isJJ,
132	                isIncluded: !excluded.contains(file.path),
133	                toggle: { toggle(file) },
134	                only: { excluded = Set(files.map(\.path)).subtracting([file.path]) })
135	            }
136	          }
137	          .padding(.vertical, 2)
138	        }
139	        .frame(maxHeight: 200)
140	        .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(.quaternary.opacity(0.4)))
141	        if isJJ {
142	          Text("jj commits the whole change. Splitting isn’t supported yet.")
143	            .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
144	        }
145	      }
146	    }
147	  }
148	
149	  /// The staged-work warning: what committing is about to throw away, named, before it happens.
150	  ///
151	  /// `git commit --only` builds from the worktree, so for a file you staged with `git add -p` and
152	  /// then kept editing, the staged version is bypassed and gone — measured, with a clean
153	  /// `git status` afterwards and no other trace. This is not a refusal (committing from a partly
154	  /// staged file is legitimate), it is the difference between an informed choice and a silent loss.
155	  private func stagedLossNotice(_ paths: [String]) -> some View {
156	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 6) {
157	      HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 8) {
158	        Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
159	          .foregroundStyle(.orange).accessibilityHidden(true)
160	        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
161	          Text(
162	            paths.count == 1
163	              ? "1 file has staged changes that differ from the file on disk"
164	              : "\(paths.count) files have staged changes that differ from the files on disk"
165	          )
166	          .font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
167	          Text(
168	            "Committing records what is on disk, so the version you staged will be replaced. "
169	              + "Stage and commit it from the terminal instead if you meant to keep it."
170	          )
171	          .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
172	          .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
173	          Text(paths.prefix(5).joined(separator: ", ") + (paths.count > 5 ? ", …" : ""))
174	            .font(.system(.caption2, design: .monospaced))
175	            .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
176	            .textSelection(.enabled)
177	            .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
178	        }
179	      }
180	    }
181	    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
182	    .padding(10)
183	    .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(Color.orange.opacity(0.08)))
184	    .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
185	    .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.stagedLoss")
186	  }
187	
188	  /// The bulk affordance. Without it, "commit only this file" — an extremely common intent — costs
189	  /// one click per unwanted file.
190	  private var selectAllRow: some View {
191	    let allIncluded = excluded.isEmpty
192	    return Button {
193	      excluded = allIncluded ? Set(files.map(\.path)) : []
194	    } label: {
195	      HStack(spacing: 6) {
196	        Image(
197	          systemName: allIncluded
198	            ? "checkmark.square.fill" : (selectedFiles.isEmpty ? "square" : "minus.square.fill")
199	        )
200	        .font(.callout)
201	        .foregroundStyle(allIncluded || !selectedFiles.isEmpty ? Color.accentColor : .secondary)
202	        .frame(width: 14)
203	        Text(allIncluded ? "Deselect all" : "Select all").font(.caption)
204	        Spacer(minLength: 0)
205	      }
206	      .contentShape(Rectangle())
207	    }
208	    .buttonStyle(.plain)
209	    .help("Include or exclude every changed file")
210	    .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.selectAll")
211	  }
212	
213	  private func toggle(_ file: ChangedFile) {
214	    if excluded.contains(file.path) {
215	      excluded.remove(file.path)
216	    } else {
217	      excluded.insert(file.path)
218	    }
219	  }
220	
221	  // MARK: Message
222	
223	  private var messageSection: some View {
224	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
225	      TextField("Summary", text: $summary)
226	        .textFieldStyle(.roundedBorder)
227	        .focused($summaryFocused)
228	        .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.summary")
229	        .onSubmit { if blockedReason == nil { commitChecking(mode: .commit) } }
230	      ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) {
231	        // SwiftUI's TextEditor has no placeholder, so it is drawn behind. `allowsHitTesting(false)`
232	        // keeps the click through to the editor.
233	        if messageBody.isEmpty {
234	          Text("Description (optional)")
235	            .font(.body)
236	            .foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
237	            .padding(.horizontal, 5)
238	            .padding(.vertical, 8)
239	            .allowsHitTesting(false)
240	        }
241	        TextEditor(text: $messageBody)
242	          .font(.body)
243	          .scrollContentBackground(.hidden)
244	          .frame(minHeight: 80, maxHeight: 140)
245	          .padding(2)
246	          .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.description")
247	      }
248	      .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(.quaternary.opacity(0.4)))
249	      .overlay(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).stroke(theme.tokens.border, lineWidth: 1))
250	    }
251	  }
252	
253	  // MARK: Buttons
254	
255	  private var buttons: some View {
256	    HStack(spacing: 8) {
257	      // A persistent line, never a tooltip: nobody hovers a button that looks dead, and a tooltip is
258	      // unreachable by keyboard and invisible to VoiceOver.
259	      if let blockedReason, phase == .editing {
260	        Text(blockedReason)
261	          .font(.caption)
262	          .foregroundStyle(.secondary)
263	          .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
264	          .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.blocked")
265	      }
266	      if phase == .committing {
267	        ProgressView().controlSize(.small)
268	        Text("Running hooks…").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
269	      }
270	      Spacer(minLength: 0)
271	      Button("Cancel") { onDismiss() }
272	        .keyboardShortcut(.cancelAction)
273	        .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.cancel")
274	      secondaryButton
275	      Button(primaryLabel) {
276	        // Once the warning is on screen the same button confirms it — the guard has already told the
277	        // user what it is about to replace, so a second warning would just be a speed bump.
278	        if case .confirmingStagedLoss = phase {
279	          commit(mode: .commit)
280	        } else {
281	          commitChecking(mode: .commit)
282	        }
283	      }
284	      .keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)
285	      .buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)
286	      .disabled(blockedReason != nil || phase == .committing)
287	      .help(isJJ ? "Describe this change and start a new one on top" : "Commit the selected files")
288	      .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.commit")
289	    }
290	  }
291	
292	  /// The backend's second verb, as its own button rather than behind a menu.
293	  ///
294	  /// There is exactly ONE alternative per backend, and a menu holding a single item is a click that
295	  /// buys nothing — it hides the choice behind a disclosure and gives the control no name until you
296	  /// open it. Naming it outright also stops the "same shape, opposite contract" problem an ellipsis
297	  /// split button would have had beside `MergeButton`, whose menu CHANGES what its primary does
298	  /// rather than performing a second action.
299	  ///
300	  /// The label is the command for jj — "Describe" is the verb jj users already have — with what it
301	  /// actually does in the help text, since the two verbs differ in a way the word alone can't carry.
302	  @ViewBuilder private var secondaryButton: some View {
303	    Button(isJJ ? "Describe" : "Amend last commit") {
304	      commit(mode: isJJ ? .describe : .amendMessage)
305	    }
306	    .disabled(phase == .committing || summary.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces).isEmpty)
307	    .help(
308	      isJJ
309	        ? "Set this change’s message and stay on it, instead of starting a new change (jj describe)"
310	        : "Replace the last commit’s message. Nothing else about that commit changes."
311	    )
312	    .accessibilityIdentifier(isJJ ? "commit.describe" : "commit.amend")
313	  }
314	
315	  // MARK: Actions
316	
317	  /// Prefill from jj's `@` description, once. git has nothing to prefill from.
318	  ///
319	  /// Reads the FULL description rather than `JJCommitChanges.description`, which is only its first
320	  /// line — prefilling the summary from that and then pressing Set Message Only would silently
321	  /// discard the body the user wrote earlier.
322	  private func prefill() {
323	    summaryFocused = true
324	    guard isJJ, !prefilled else { return }
325	    prefilled = true
326	    guard let item = store.selectedStatusWorkItem(for: pending.sid) else { return }
327	    Task {
328	      let result = await StatusCommandRunner().run(
329	        "jj", CLIVCSWriter.jjDescriptionArgs(), in: item.path, timeout: 5)
330	      guard result.ok else { return }
331	      let existing = CommitDraft.split(message: result.stdout)
332	      // Never clobber something typed while the read was in flight.
333	      if summary.isEmpty && messageBody.isEmpty {
334	        summary = existing.summary
335	        messageBody = existing.body
336	      }
337	    }
338	  }
339	
340	  /// Commit, but check first whether doing so would throw away staged work.
341	  ///
342	  /// Only for the plain git commit path: amend takes no pathspec, and jj has no index. The check is
343	  /// skipped once confirmed so pressing "Commit anyway" cannot re-raise the same warning.
344	  private func commitChecking(mode: VCSCommitMode) {
345	    guard phase == .editing, mode == .commit, !isJJ else { return commit(mode: mode) }
346	    let files = selectedFiles
347	    store.stagedContentAtRisk(on: pending.sid, files: files) { atRisk in
348	      if atRisk.isEmpty {
349	        commit(mode: mode)
350	      } else {
351	        phase = .confirmingStagedLoss(atRisk)
352	      }
353	    }
354	  }
355	
356	  private func commit(mode: VCSCommitMode) {
357	    guard phase != .committing else { return }
358	    phase = .committing
359	    let request = VCSCommitRequest(
360	      message: CommitDraft.message(summary: summary, body: messageBody),
361	      files: mode == .amendMessage ? [] : selectedFiles, mode: mode)
362	    store.performCommit(request, on: pending.sid) { result in
363	      switch result {
364	      case .ok:
365	        onDismiss()
366	      case .committedThenFailed(_, let detail):
367	        // The commit LANDED. Closing would be a lie by omission, and offering a retry would create a
368	        // second commit, so the sheet stays up saying exactly that.
369	        phase = .failed(
370	          VCSFailureDialog(
371	            title: "Committed, but something afterwards failed",
372	            message:
373	              "The commit was recorded. A step that runs after it — usually a post-commit hook — "
374	              + "then failed. Do not commit again; the change is already saved.",
375	            details: detail, recovery: nil, lockPath: nil))
376	      case .failed(let failure):
377	        phase = .failed(VCSSyncPresenter.commitFailureDialog(failure, mode: mode))
378	      }
379	    }
380	  }
381	}

383	/// One changed file, with its inclusion checkbox.
384	///
385	/// The checkbox is an SF Symbol in a 14pt slot rather than a `Toggle` on purpose: the row aligns on
386	/// `.firstTextBaseline` so the directory text sits on the filename's baseline, and a `Toggle` has no
387	/// text baseline to align to — it would sit visibly high against the change letter beside it. Same
388	/// glyph size and same slot width as that letter, so both share a baseline by construction.
389	private struct CommitFileRow: View {
390	  let file: ChangedFile
391	  let showsCheckbox: Bool
392	  let isIncluded: Bool
393	  let toggle: () -> Void
394	  let only: () -> Void
395	  private let theme = ThemeService.shared
396	
397	  var body: some View {
398	    HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 6) {
399	      if showsCheckbox {
400	        Button(action: toggle) {
401	          Image(systemName: isIncluded ? "checkmark.square.fill" : "square")
402	            .font(.callout)
403	            .foregroundStyle(isIncluded ? Color.accentColor : .secondary)
404	            .frame(width: 14)
405	        }
406	        .buttonStyle(.plain)
407	        .help(isIncluded ? "Exclude this file from the commit" : "Include this file in the commit")
408	        .accessibilityLabel("\(file.path), \(isIncluded ? "included" : "excluded")")
409	        .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.file.check.\(file.path)")
410	      }
411	      // Combined SEPARATELY from the checkbox, not across the whole row. An
412	      // `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)` on the row collapses everything inside it into one
413	      // element, which takes the checkbox with it — the control then isn't individually clickable and
414	      // XCUITest cannot toggle it. Caught by `CommitSheetUITests`; same family as the
415	      // `children: .contain` note on `VCSFailureSheet`.
416	      HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: 6) {
417	        Text(ChangeBadge.letter(file.change))
418	          .font(.system(.caption, design: .monospaced))
419	          .foregroundStyle(ChangeBadge.color(file.change, theme.tokens))
420	          .frame(width: 14)
421	        let parts = ChangesPanel.splitPath(file.path)
422	        Text(parts.name).font(.callout).lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.middle)
423	        if !parts.dir.isEmpty {
424	          Text(parts.dir)
425	            .font(.caption2).foregroundStyle(.tertiary)
426	            .lineLimit(1).truncationMode(.head)
427	        }
428	        Spacer(minLength: 0)
429	      }
430	      .accessibilityElement(children: .combine)
431	      .accessibilityLabel("\(ChangeBadge.word(file.change)) \(file.path)")
432	    }
433	    .padding(.horizontal, 8)
434	    .padding(.vertical, 2)
435	    // Excluded rows dim their CONTENT rather than taking a background: the accent background already
436	    // means "this row's diff is the focused tab" in the Changes panel, and two selection meanings
437	    // sharing one visual is how a user learns to distrust both.
438	    .opacity(showsCheckbox && !isIncluded ? 0.45 : 1)
439	    .contentShape(Rectangle())
440	    // `.contain`, never `.combine`: the row holds two things a user acts on separately — the
441	    // checkbox and the file — and combining them would merge the checkbox into the row, leaving no
442	    // individually clickable control. The label halves live on the two children instead.
443	    .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
444	    .contextMenu {
445	      if showsCheckbox {
446	        Button("Commit Only This File", action: only)
447	        Button(isIncluded ? "Exclude This File" : "Include This File", action: toggle)
448	      }
449	    }
450	  }
451	}

453	/// A commit failure, inline. Same content as `VCSFailureSheet` — a sheet cannot present another
454	/// sheet over itself, and the draft has to stay on screen because it survives the failure.
455	private struct CommitFailureNotice: View {
456	  let dialog: VCSFailureDialog
457	  @State private var showDetails = false
458	
459	  var body: some View {
460	    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 8) {
461	      HStack(alignment: .top, spacing: 8) {
462	        Image(systemName: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill")
463	          .foregroundStyle(.orange)
464	          .accessibilityHidden(true)
465	        VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 4) {
466	          Text(dialog.title).font(.subheadline.weight(.semibold))
467	          Text(dialog.message)
468	            .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)
469	            .textSelection(.enabled)
470	            .fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)
471	        }
472	      }
473	      // The hook's own output is the most useful text in the whole taxonomy — 40 lines of eslint
474	      // naming file and line — so it gets a scroll pane and selectable text, not a truncated line.
475	      if let details = dialog.details {
476	        DisclosureGroup(isExpanded: $showDetails) {
477	          ScrollView {
478	            Text(details)
479	              .font(.system(.caption2, design: .monospaced))
480	              .textSelection(.enabled)
481	              .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
482	              .padding(6)
483	          }
484	          .frame(maxHeight: 120)
485	          .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 5).fill(.quaternary.opacity(0.5)))
486	        } label: {
487	          Text("Output").font(.caption.weight(.semibold))
488	        }
489	        .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.failure.detailsToggle")
490	      }
491	    }
492	    .frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .leading)
493	    .padding(10)
494	    .background(RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: 6).fill(Color.orange.opacity(0.08)))
495	    .accessibilityElement(children: .contain)
496	    .accessibilityIdentifier("commit.failure")
497	  }
498	}

This is a pure UI refactor: `Menu`-with-one-item → single `Button`. Both branches call the identical `commit(mode:)` with the same modes (`.describe` for jj, `.amendMessage` for git). The `disabled` predicate is unchanged, help text is equivalent, and only the accessibility identifier changed from `commit.moreActions` to `commit.describe`/`commit.amend`.

No new sinks, no new data-flow paths, no changes to `commit()`, `commitChecking()`, or any command builder. The test file only adds XCUITest assertions on the new buttons.

Checking against my heuristics:
- No shell/exec/SQL/path/URL sinks introduced.
- No permission/gate/allowlist logic touched.
- No log/telemetry sinks with new fields.
- No parser/validator differentials — pure boolean `isJJ` split.
- No teardown/identity mapping changes.
- No a11y-id fanout risk: the old id (`commit.moreActions`) is not searched for outside this file's tests.
Only the two files in this diff reference the identifiers — no stale references elsewhere. No security implications.
